    Simultaneous Hom-rank realization in a rational torsion chamber #

    Key step for Proposition 2.5(1): given a module B strictly positive on nonzero quotients and a module M strictly negative on nonzero subobjects at the Euler weight of P, some positive multiple of [P] admits a ground-field differential that is simultaneously surjective on Hom(-, B) and injective on Hom(-, M) (exists_block_precomposition_tests), proved via max-rank specialization over k̄ and restriction of scalars from a finite field extension.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.strict_expansion_of_subobject_neg (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (P : TwoTerm R) (M : FGModuleCat R) (neg : ∀ {T : FGModuleCat R} (i : T ⟶ M) [CategoryTheory.Mono i], ¬CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero T → (eulerWeight k P).eval T < 0) (U : Submodule k (P.target ⟶ M)) (V : Submodule k (P.source ⟶ M)) (h : ∀ (p : P.source ⟶ P.target) (f : ↥U), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp p ↑f ∈ V) (hu : 0 < Module.finrank k ↥U) :
    Module.finrank k ↥U < Module.finrank k ↥V

    Strict negativity on every nonzero subobject forces strict expansion of each nonzero space of maps from the target projective.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.exists_block_precomposition_tests (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (P : TwoTerm R) (B M : FGModuleCat R) (pos : ∀ {Q : FGModuleCat R} (p : B ⟶ Q) [CategoryTheory.Epi p], ¬CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero Q → 0 < (eulerWeight k P).eval Q) (neg : ∀ {U : FGModuleCat R} (i : U ⟶ M) [CategoryTheory.Mono i], ¬CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero U → (eulerWeight k P).eval U < 0) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : 0 < n) (Q : TwoTerm R), Q.projectiveClass = n • P.projectiveClass ∧ Function.Surjective ⇑(Q.precompose B) ∧ Function.Injective ⇑(Q.precompose M)

    For a module positive on its nonzero quotients and a module negative on its nonzero subobjects, a common ground differential has the two required Hom ranks. The class is a positive multiple of the original projective class.
